newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended lower on Thursday on sustained profit-taking in selected blue chips, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed 1.56 points lower, or 0.22 percent, at 691.98 points after touching an intra-day low of 689.65 points. Losers led gainers by 62 to 59 with 71 issues unchanged. Total turn-over was estimated at 460 billion rupiah, compared with 563 billion rupiah on Wednesday.
Brokers said the market was likely to remain in negative territory on Friday as investors cash out ahead of the weekend.
"Some stocks which are taking corporate action such as Bank Negara Indonesia might continue making gains or become targets of profit-takers," one local broker said.
Despite the rampant profit taking, buying interest was seen in blue chips Sampoerna and Indosat, brokers said.

Foreign-led buying interest was seen in cigarette firm PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna on what brokers said was due to market talk that Sampoerna majority shareholder, Putera Sampoerna, had intentions to buy a stake in property firm PT Surya Semesta Internusa.
Surya Semesta fell in active trading on profit-taking after sharp gains last week on market talk of the possible entry of new investor in the firm, brokers said.
Sampoerna and Surya officials were not available for comment. But an analyst with an European firm doubted the rumours had boosted sentiment on Sampoerna.

"I think its more a technical rebound after Sampoerna share prices were dampened by opinion that its first quarter net profit was lower than market expectations. In fact, its net profit was comparatively higher," the analyst said.

Indosat was also active on fresh buying. Brokers said improved sentiment on the counter was linked to news that it had just launched a new international telecommunication service using the International Maritime Satellite Network (Inmarsat).
Bank BNI topped the active list with 42.6 million shares traded as it ended 25 rupiah higher at 1,650 rupiah after an intra-day high of 1,675 rupiah earlier.
Brokers said BNI shares peaked on market talk that the bank would announce a corporate plan. "Prices waned on profit-taking after BNI announced it will buy a stake in a bank," one said.
The bank said in a statement that it intends to purchase shares owned by Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, in N.V. De Indonesische Overzeese Bank (Indover) in Amsterdam.
Brokers said news that Bimantara's first quarter net profit was 17 percent higher than in the corresponding 1996 period had little impact on prices.
The market also shrugged off Bimantara's setting up of a joint venture with Hyundai Motor Corp of South Korea to produce sedans and commercial vehicles.
"The contribution of its car division to total revenue is still insignificant and the project is not new at all," an analyst said. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
